newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept retail sales data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK Sept retail sales data.

text.p: Following is a list of reactions to UK September retail sales data published at 0830 GMT.
The figures showed retail sales -0.3 percent month-on-month and +3.5 percent year-on-year. Market forecasts centred on a 0.1 percent monthly fall and year-on-year rise of 3.9 percent.

"Slightly lower than expected on face of it but positive for gilts and within the range of forecasts. The sharp fall in sales of clothing and footwear suggests some resistance on the part of consumers to accept price increases. Those prices rose particularly strongly in September."

"Figures are at the weaker end of expectations but not to the extent that would reawaken thoughts of lower interest rates. It may be significant that after two slightly firmer-than- anticipated RPI figures, sales have turned down again but the Sept figures must be seen in the context of a 0.9 percent jump in August."

"I don't really think the monthly fall is much of a big deal. The anecdotal evidence suggested a weaker monthly figure, but the longer-term trend is still upward and the year-on-year breakdowns all look quite strong across all the sectors. The consumer-led recovery is still intact and there is absolutely no room for (Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth) Clarke to cut interest rates."
MARION BELL, ROYAL BANK OF SCOTLAND

"The figures came in weaker than expected with textile, clothing and footwear sales, which fell by 3.0 percent, dragging down the overall figure. This should help the Chancellor in his attempts to keep interest rate unchanged until the election. However, the trend in retail sales remains positive."
